title: Customer-facing SLA latency rescue: runbook, priority smoothing, and hotfix rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We received a high-priority escalation from two enterprise customers (one Hosted, one Dedicated / VPC) reporting a 2-3x increase in TTFT and 30-50% drop in tokens/sec for multi-shot chat workloads across a set of quantized LLM variants. The regression started on 2026-03-09 07:20 UTC and correlates with an autoscaler rollout and a kernel selector tuning change. Immediate objective: stabilize customer traffic to meet SLA (p99 TTFT <= 450ms for short prompts), deploy a safe hotfix, and create a runbook for future cross-deployment escalations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Replay customer workload (recorded traffic) against hosted cluster region us-west-2 and a dedicated VPC cluster using the same model variant (quant-int8-llama-v3-7b).
2) Use recorded arrival patterns: short prompts (8-40 tokens context), concurrent long-polling sessions (20-120s). Observe first-token latency and sustained token/sec.
3) Toggle kernel_selector=v2 -> v1 and observe immediate restoration of tokens/sec in reproduced env.
implementation_notes:
Hypothesis: kernel_selector v2 introduced an aggressive microbatching heuristic that increases head-of-line blocking for short, primed sessions under mixed fanout. This interacts poorly with the new autoscaler that increases cold starting of small-weight shards and an updated KV prefetch timeout. Fix implemented in branch eng/459321/priority-smoother:
- Revert microbatching heuristic (fallback to v1 behavior) behind a feature flag.
- Add a short-session priority smoothing layer that hedges warmstart for requests under 50 tokens.
- Reduce KV prefetch timeout from 200ms -> 80ms when session_history_len < 64.
- Add telemetry tags to trace kernel selection and prefetch latency per request.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Canary on 1 host pool in us-west-2 for hosted traffic (2-hour canary) with 10% of traffic routed via priority-smoothing policy.
Phase 1: Expand to dedicated test VPC (customer staging) and 5% of production dedicated pools.
Phase 2: Full region rollout for hosted and coordinated push for Dedicated/Private with ops-runbook steps.
Rollback: disable feature flag and reinstate kernel_selector v1. Immediate fallback available via routing policy to model-variant-compat (non-quantized) for highly affected sessions.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Reverting microbatch heuristic may reduce throughput under high bursty long-context workloads. Mitigation: keep heuristic behind flag; enable adaptive batch sizing only for >256 token contexts. Monitor tokens/sec and queue depth metrics; autoscaler thresholds to be temporarily tightened during rollout to avoid cold start churn.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canary shows <=10% delta in p99 TTFT vs baseline within 2 hours.
- Affected customer confirms improvement and resumes normal traffic.
- No >5% regression in max sustained throughput for stress tests (20k tokens/sec per GPU shard).
- Telemetry indicates kernel selection stabilized to v1-like paths for short sessions.
testing_and_validation:
- Load tests: synthetic short-session fanout + priming patterns against canary hosts.
- Integration: run regression suite for hosted/dedicated/private configurations; validate no memory regressions under quant-int8.
- QA: customer bridge verification with two impacted customers; runbook dry run.
